# Independent audit: sharp centroid contraction cap loss

Source: `candidate 268d75cf9619baac`.

**Result: PASS, all dimensions d>=1 and every proper cap.** The independent
verifier `supporting computation verify_sharp_centroid_cap_loss_slab_recovery.py` passes 960 exact
checks: actual convex-polygon losses, both signed moment terms, and cone
identities through dimension twelve. These supplement the full proof
below. No mixed-integer conclusion is inferred without the separately
stated weighted and source-gap hypotheses.

## 1. Differentiability and global cap-root tangent

At every threshold strictly between the two support extremes, the convex
body's section has positive (d-1)-volume. For d>=2, section-root concavity
from ordinary Brunn--Minkowski makes the section density continuous there.
For d=1 it is exactly 1/||v||. Thus the cap-volume derivative at the cut
is -sigma with the coarea factor exactly as stated. The homothety formula
is differentiable at zero and yields L_g=dU+(b-v.g)sigma.

Convex combinations of the two actual truncated bodies lie in the
interpolated truncation, including when a truncation is the whole A.
Therefore F^(1/d) is concave on (-infinity,h), including its constant
left portion. Its proper-cut tangent bounds it from above on BOTH sides
of zero. If h>D=dU/sigma, a point between D and h would have positive
cap root but a negative upper tangent, which is impossible. This
justifies the upper-support bound without assuming equality of supports.

On [D(1-s),0], where s=(a/U)^(1/d)>1, the tangent is nonnegative and
its dth power is at most a. Consequently a-F is bounded from below by
a minus that dth power. This is the required negative-tail estimate;
it is not an erroneous reversal of the tangent inequality. Together
these observations give the global survival domination

    F(t)<=G(t),
    G(t)=a for t<=D(1-s),
         U(1-t/D)^d for D(1-s)<=t<=D,
         0 for t>=D.

## 2. Signed moment and exact constant

The scalar coordinate is v.x-b and its mean is mu=v.g-b. Positive and
negative layer cake give exactly

    a*mu=integral_0^infinity F
                   -integral_(-infinity)^0(a-F).

All integrals are finite, and hyperplane sections are d-volume null even
in d=1. The proof bounds the positive term above and subtracts a lower
bound on a subinterval of the negative term. Its sign is therefore
correct. Direct integration gives a*mu<=aD[1-ds/(d+1)]. Multiplication
by sigma and sigma*D=dU yields

    L_g>=d^2/(d+1)*U*s
       =d^2/(d+1)*a^(1/d)*U^((d-1)/d).

Every power is applied to positive U. For d=1 the result is a/2 for all
proper interval cuts, with no undefined zero power.

For complete center bookkeeping, g lies in A because an exterior
separating functional would contradict v.g=average_A(v.x)<=h_A(v).
The source's supporting-functional mean argument then excludes boundary
points and gives g in int A. Thus all contractions are actual nested
convex bodies about the same admissible point g.

## 3. Sharpness and simultaneous weights

The cone with base at D(1-s) and apex at D has precisely survival function
G. Choosing its base measure fixes any desired total a in dimension at
least two; choosing interval length does the same in dimension one.
The cut at zero is proper for every s>1. Both signed-tail inequalities
are equalities, proving sharpness at every fraction U/a in (0,1).

The same actual centroid is used for every cap, so nonnegative weighted
summation is valid without optimizing losses at different points. For
planar normalized weights pi_i this gives
Lbar(g)>=(4/3)a sum pi_i sqrt(U_i/a). The threshold 1/3 implies the
previous sufficient loss 4a/9 exactly. The ordinary theorem does not
force this weighted threshold or eliminate tied endpoint sources; the
source retains those limitations.

## 4. Optional complete equality classification

The proof also gives the following rigorous equality statement, using
no equality theorem for Brunn--Minkowski:

> Equality for one proper cap holds if and only if A is a cone with one
> apex on its maximum support plane and base on its minimum support
> plane, both planes parallel to the cut. In dimension one this means
> an interval, so equality always holds.

Here a cone means the convex hull of one point and a full-dimensional
convex base in the parallel (d-1)-plane; its apex need not project to a
special point of that base.

Proof. F and G are continuous survival functions of bounded nonatomic
scalar laws, and F<=G everywhere. Their signed mean difference is
integral_R(G-F)/a. If equality holds in the cap-loss bound, this mean
difference is zero. Nonnegativity and continuity imply F=G at every
level. Positivity of proper section densities then identifies the actual
support endpoints as t0=D(1-s) and D.

Choose an ACTUAL point p in A with scalar coordinate D. For 0<r<1,
convexity gives

    p+r(A-p) subset A intersect {t>=D+r(t0-D)}=:C_r.

Both sides have volume r^d*a, since the cap survival is exactly G.
Inclusion of full convex bodies with equal volume is equality: if a
point of the larger compact convex body lay outside the smaller closed
one, its convex hull with an interior ball of the smaller would supply
positive extra volume. Thus C_r=p+r(A-p).

The whole maximum support face lies in every C_r, whose diameter is
r*diam(A). Letting r decrease to zero proves that this face is the
singleton p. For any other x in A, put r=(D-t(x))/(D-t0), which lies
in (0,1]. The equality of caps gives x=p+r(z-p) for some z in A.
Its scalar coordinate forces t(z)=t0. Thus every point belongs to the
convex hull of p and the minimum face. The reverse inclusion is convexity.
The minimum face has dimension d-1 because A has interior. Hence A is
exactly the stated cone. The converse is the already checked cone-tail
formula. This classifies equality for one direction without asserting
simultaneous equality for an arbitrary cap family.
